sections.development: The preacher alone: the lead's call, the organ's answer, the lead's answer, the choir's hum; Fm, Db, then C7 and a breath.
The drop on V2's own pocket: the V3 hook as a four-bar question and answer, the climb, the peak, V2's hole.
Room for a voice: a new 808 line (Fm Fm Db C); the lead only tags the end of each four-bar line; a hum enters halfway.
The second hook: the lead calls F-Ab-C, a few singers answer Eb-Db-C, the organ echoes; Db Eb Fm C.
More pressure (stutter kicks, sixteenth hats, octave hops); then a half-time floor and one stop-time on the second hook.
No drums, no 808: the choir alone (Bbm9, the Neapolitan Gb, C7b9), then the organ and Pedal and the lead's cry.
The ceiling opens: the lead calls with the first hook, the full choir answers with the second, full-organ hits.
V2's amen groove and dive; Db, C7, then F major; the lead bends its Ab up to A.
